ranking.note: Promoted: only PR here that fixes a reproducible node crash (assertion in TestBlockValidity) reachable from an external mining client during startup/reindex; stability outranks the feature work.
Kept P2 but moved up: a live data race between submitSolution and template reads (issue #36515) is the most correctness-relevant item after the crash fix.
Same band, placed behind the correctness fixes and behind #35581, whose BlockTemplateManager it builds on; it is visibility/accounting, not a fix.
Moved up within P3: signed overflow in cluster fee arithmetic silently drops prioritised transactions from templates, which touches template correctness, the category's top concern.
Demoted: reviewers and the author agree the no-mempool lookup path is unreachable in production, so this is a contract tidy-up with no user-visible consequence.
Demoted: regtest-only convenience for generateblock, narrow and speculative next to the other developer tooling here (#30437 at least exercises the production IPC path).

inconsistencies: Chain: #35581 introduces BlockTemplateManager; #33922 (weak-pointer template tracking) and #36356/#36357 (moving statics into BlockTemplateManager) all assume that class. Review #35581 first or the three will diverge on the manager's shape and ownership rules.
Chain: #36356 is the stated base of #36357 and (together with #36921) of #36922. Review order should be #36921 and #36356, then #36357, then #36922.

#36870 (steady clock in WaitAndCreateNewBlock) and #36922 (steady clock for the getblocktemplate rebuild interval) fix the same class of wall-clock-vs-mocktime bug in two places; reviewing them together would settle one convention instead of two. #36870 should go first as it affects the IPC waitNext path used in production.

#36525, #36097 and #35300 each make breaking changes to the Mining capnp interface (Block handle, cancellation arguments, precious ordinal deprecation). Merging them in an uncoordinated order forces repeated client updates on sv2-tp; #36525 is the one with a bug behind it and should be settled first.
#36097 carries a temporary libmultiprocess subtree commit (upstream PR 342) and #36870 depends on #36862; neither dependency is in this category, so their readiness is gated outside mining.

#36940 (NaN/negative timeouts) and #36132 (no-mempool lookups) are both hardening of paths no current client reaches; they are ranked adjacent-ish rather than one being treated as a real bug and the other as theoretical — #36940 stays higher only because it aborts debug builds.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: one crash fix (P1), a cluster of Mining-interface/IPC capability and correctness work driven by Stratum v2 consumers (P2), a long tail of global-state cleanups, clock-source fixes and test repairs (P3), and two marginal items (P4). Several P3s are stages of the same BlockTemplateManager refactor, so their value is largely in the order they land.
